hotspots.whyItMatters: Direct crossover with NEC 250.52 grounding electrodes. Whether a rebar electrode qualifies depends on concrete placement practice.
hotspots.cite: Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures. Confirm chapter in your copy. Cross-check NEC 250.52(A)(3)
hotspots.trap: Assuming any rebar touching the ground qualifies as a concrete-encased electrode without the code's minimum-length, encasement, and earth-contact conditions being met.

hotspots.whyItMatters: Curing time and conditions affect when it's safe to disturb embedded raceways or electrodes.
hotspots.cite: Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures. Confirm chapter in your copy
hotspots.trap: Disturbing or loading a slab/footing with embedded electrical work before adequate cure strength is reached.

hotspots.topic: Mix design basics relevant to sign/structural footings
hotspots.whyItMatters: Ties back into the sign-structures subject cluster: footings for pole and monument signs.
hotspots.cite: Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures. Confirm chapter in your copy
hotspots.trap: Specifying a footing by volume/depth alone without regard to the mix strength the structural design actually assumes.
